introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A discrete variable, $X$, has the following probability distribution

| $x$ | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X=x)$ | $\dfrac{2}{15}$ | $\dfrac15$ | $\dfrac{4}{15}$ | $k$ | $\dfrac16$ |

Find (a) the value of $k$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The probabilities of a distribution add up to $1$:

$$\frac2{15}+\frac15+\frac4{15}+k+\frac16=1.$$

Common denominator $30$: $\dfrac4{30}+\dfrac6{30}+\dfrac8{30}+k+\dfrac5{30}=1$, so $\dfrac{23}{30}+k=1$.

$$k=1-\frac{23}{30}=\frac7{30}.$$

**$k=\dfrac7{30}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) the mean and variance of the distribution. *[4 marks]*

(ii) In a tray of eggs, 4 out of 8 are found to be bad.

(a) Find the probability of selecting a bad egg at random from the tray. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$$P(\text{bad egg})=\frac{\text{number of bad eggs}}{\text{total number of eggs}}=\frac48=\frac12.$$

**$P(\text{bad})=\dfrac12$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that 5 eggs are selected at random from the tray, using the binomial distribution, find

(ii)(b) the probability that no bad egg was selected. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $Y$ be the number of bad eggs among the $5$ selected: $Y\sim B(n=5,\ p=\tfrac12)$, so $q=\tfrac12$. Use $P(Y=r)=\binom nr p^rq^{n-r}$ with $r=0$:

$$P(Y=0)=\binom50\left(\frac12\right)^0\left(\frac12\right)^5=\frac1{32}=0.03125.$$

**$P(\text{no bad egg})=\dfrac1{32}\approx0.031$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) the mean and standard deviation of the binomial distribution. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $B(n,p)$: mean $=np$ and variance $=npq$.

Mean $=5\times\dfrac12=2.5$.

Variance $=5\times\dfrac12\times\dfrac12=1.25$, so the standard deviation is $\sqrt{1.25}=\dfrac{\sqrt5}2\approx1.118$.

**Mean $=2.5$; standard deviation $\approx1.12$.**
